answer: The 220-row consolidated matrix (`docs/architecture/hyperscaler-pattern-attribution.md`) is hyperscaler-fit at the portfolio level: every keystone-bundle decision (ADR-0242..ADR-0255) carries a named pattern + source + anti-pattern triple, multi-source citation density is ≈95%, 2024-2026 source share is ≈40%, and the 5 novel primitives are each composed from hyperscaler-precedented sub-primitives with documented why-novel-but-defensible justifications. However, the bundle is NOT yet self-consistent across the cross-check scope: ADR-0258 / ADR-0272 / ADR-0273 / ADR-0276 / ADR-0292 author Appendix A in NARRATIVE prose form, not the canonical 4-column matrix shape mandated by §2.2 + §8.1 of the attribution doctrine, and NONE of ADR-0255-amendment / ADR-0257 / ADR-0263 / ADR-0272 / ADR-0273 / ADR-0276 / ADR-0280 / ADR-0284 / ADR-0292 has been appended to §3 of the consolidated matrix — directly violating §8.1 step 2 ('Add a new §3.X subsection ... in the same commit'). The §6 scorecard claims ADR-0244 has 18 rows but the §3.3 table shows 16 visible rows plus 2 sub-rows (D-1.r, D-2.d); §3 preamble says '205 rows' but §6 aggregate says '220 rows' — internal drift. The novel-primitive checks (§5) pass for 4/5; BYOK-everywhere (§5.5) is the weakest: SecretReference unification is only *partially* novel — Stripe Connect's BYOK Secret pattern + Vault Transit's owner-declared-key abstraction already approximate it, and the §5.5 'no hyperscaler offers a unified BYOK across every secret class' claim is over-stated relative to HashiCorp Vault Transit's actual surface. Weak-citation rows: 11 identified (5%, within §6's stated tolerance). Citation freshness for 2024-2026 sources is genuinely strong (Stripe Cells 2024, Pingora 2024, X25519MLKEM768 2024, Bedrock 2024, Azure AI Foundry 2024, GPT-4o 2024-05, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 2024-06, Gemini 1.5 Pro 2024-02, AWS Aurora DSQL re:Invent 2024, AWS 2024 ARC404/ARC405, Cloudflare HTTP/3, NIST FIPS 203 2024). Stripe Engineering Quora 2013 (cited at ADR-0242 D-1) is the one stale-link risk explicitly acknowledged by §7.2. ADR-0258 / ADR-0272 / ADR-0292's narrative Appendix A is harder to audit and should be normalized to the matrix shape OR the maintenance protocol (§8.1) should be amended to admit narrative form for compliance-overlay ADRs.

§5.1 (Foundry dissolution): novelty claim is DEFENSIBLE. Hyperscaler precedent for *dissolving* a Foundry-equivalent µservice does not exist publicly; AWS Bedrock absorption of provider adapters is the closest analogue, correctly distinguished as consumer-facing. The 4-bullet F2 checklist is fully completed in the document.

§5.2 (Intelligence-as-substrate two-layer): novelty claim is DEFENSIBLE. AWS Bedrock + Apple Intelligence composition is correctly cited; the audience-as-Cedar-context-attribute (not service-boundary) extension genuinely closes the no-bypass-paths-for-platform-owner property ADR-0242 demands. F2 checklist complete.

§5.3 (oyatie-as-tenant slug): novelty claim is DEFENSIBLE. Stripe's SOC 2 covering Stripe's internal use is the closest analogue but at a different layer (Stripe paying contractors via Stripe), correctly distinguished. The Compliance-Carve-Out anti-pattern is real and load-bearing — no hyperscaler has *publicly documented* their platform-owner account fully participating in SOC 2 + GDPR DSAR + audit-chain machinery.

§5.4 (Compliance Pack abstraction): novelty claim is DEFENSIBLE. AWS Audit Manager + Google Assured Workloads + Microsoft Purview correctly cited as closest precedents; the pack-as-installable-bundle with deterministic-lifecycle + Cedar-fragments + onboarding-workflow + breach-notification + DPIA-template + retention-semantics is a genuine composition not present in any single hyperscaler. The mechanical-operability worked example in ADR-0251 Appendix B is strong evidence.

§5.5 (BYOK-everywhere): novelty claim is THE WEAKEST of the five. HashiCorp Vault Transit + Vault Secrets Operator already provides much of the 'unified BYOK across every secret class' surface — Vault's `transit` engine wraps LLM API keys, payment processor keys, KMS keys, and storage encryption keys behind a single SecretReference-equivalent abstraction with policy-driven access. The §5.5 claim 'No hyperscaler offers a unified BYOK abstraction across every secret class' is technically true for the AWS/GCP/Azure cloud-vendor BYOK surfaces but over-states relative to Vault Transit. RECOMMENDATION: re-frame §5.5 to claim 'unified BYOK + Cedar-context-driven selection at dispatch time' as the novel piece (Vault Transit does NOT integrate Cedar-style policy at the dispatch boundary), and demote the broader 'no hyperscaler offers unified BYOK' claim.

5.1_foundry_dissolution.weakness: The 'no hyperscaler has publicly dissolved their equivalent' claim is unverifiable in the negative — F2 cannot prove a hyperscaler hasn't done so privately. 5.2_intelligence_as_substrate_two_layer.weakness: Apple Intelligence's substrate+brand-surface separation is inferred from WWDC 2024 keynote behavior, not from a published architecture diagram. Citation is correct but the precedent is partly reverse-engineered. Acceptable but worth flagging.

Microsoft Graph internal first-party tenants DO participate in Microsoft's SOC 2 boundary in some configurations. The novelty claim could be sharpened to 'fully + UNIFORMLY + with no administrative carve-out' rather than 'fully audited' which is partly precedented.

FedRAMP High ⊇ Moderate hierarchical certification inheritance
5.4_compliance_pack_abstraction.weakness: Salesforce HealthCloud and GovCloud SKUs are closer to 'installable-bundle' shape than the doctrine acknowledges. The ADR-0251 D-1 row cites them, but §5.4 framing 'they typically don't package the full regulation as an installable pack with its own lifecycle' is over-stated for Salesforce HealthCloud which IS lifecycle-managed. Sharpen the claim to 'no hyperscaler ships ALL FIVE: Cedar fragments + onboarding workflow + breach-notification workflow + DPIA template + retention semantics in one bundle' — that is the genuinely novel composition.

composed_hyperscaler_patterns: AWS Bedrock CMK + Azure Key Vault CMK + GCP CMEK BYOK pattern (per-substrate)
HashiCorp Vault Transit (universal-secret abstraction; the strongest precedent)
5.5_byok_everywhere.weakness: THIS IS THE WEAKEST NOVELTY CLAIM IN THE BUNDLE. HashiCorp Vault Transit ALREADY provides a unified BYOK-everywhere abstraction across secret classes via the `transit` engine + per-secret access policies. The §5.5 framing 'No hyperscaler offers a unified BYOK abstraction across every secret class' is technically defensible only if Vault Transit is excluded from 'hyperscaler' — but Vault is the de-facto standard secret substrate. The genuine novelty is 'Cedar-driven selection at dispatch time' (Vault uses Vault policies, not Cedar; oyatie unifies under one policy engine per ADR-0243). RECOMMENDATION: re-frame §5.5 to claim the novelty as 'unified BYOK SecretReference + Cedar-driven dispatch-time selection (not Vault-policy or per-substrate IAM)', and demote the broader 'no hyperscaler' claim.

matrix_maintenance_scaling: The matrix is 2527 lines and 220 rows; maintenance burden grows linearly with ADR count. §8 protocol delegates ownership to council-architecture; at the current rate of ~10 new ADRs per quarter (extrapolated from ADR-0242..ADR-0292 span ~3 months), the matrix will hit ~300 rows by end of 2026.

CI lane `oya-check-hyperscaler-pattern-matrix-coherence` must be fast-path (per-PR sub-second) given matrix growth; recommend pre-computed row-index cached in `.omc/cache/` to avoid full re-scan per PR.

Per-source-bucket density audits (§4) are currently visual; at >300 rows the visual audit breaks down. Recommend §4 buckets be auto-generated from §3 rows by a generator script (`tools/generate-matrix-source-buckets.sh`), eliminating drift between §3 and §4.
novel_primitive_review_scaling: Each novel primitive requires 4-bullet defensibility checklist + worked example + 'why no hyperscaler precedent' literature review. At 5 novel primitives today, this is tractable; at 20+ it becomes a serious documentation tax.
Recommend §5 cap: portfolio admits at most N novel primitives at any time (suggested N=10); promotion of a 6th requires retiring or deprecating an existing one. Forces architectural discipline.

summary_for_synthesis: F2 verdict: APPROVE-WITH-FINDINGS. The 220-row consolidated matrix is hyperscaler-fit at the portfolio level (95% multi-source density; 41% 2024-2026 freshness; 100% named-pattern coverage; anti-patterns load-bearing and genuine). The 5 novel primitives are 4/5 strong (Foundry dissolution, Intelligence-as-substrate, oyatie-as-tenant slug, Compliance Pack abstraction); BYOK-everywhere is the weakest claim and should be sharpened to acknowledge HashiCorp Vault Transit precedent. Critical findings: (1) consolidated matrix preamble row-count drifts from §6 aggregate (205 vs 220); (2) extended-scope ADRs (ADR-0257, ADR-0263, ADR-0272-0292) carry Appendix A but are NOT appended to §3 — §8.1 violation; (3) ADR-0258/0272/0273/0276/0292 use narrative-form Appendix A bypassing the CI lane regex; (4) 11 weak-citation rows identified within §6 tolerance. 17 fixuptasks proposed (1 S1, 6 S2, 8 S3, 2 S4).
